bones.name: c2disc
bones.function: Fibrocartilaginous pad interposed between the adjacent surfaces of the bodies of C2 and C3, forming one of the chief bonds of connection between the vertebrae. Like all discs it is built of concentric laminae of fibrous tissue and fibrocartilage (the annulus fibrosus) around a soft, highly elastic nucleus pulposus, and acts as an important shock absorber. In the cervical region the discs are thicker in front than behind, contributing to the anterior convexity (lordosis) of the neck.
bones.note: The uppermost disc of the whole column: the series of intervertebral fibrocartilages extends only from the axis to the sacrum, so there is no disc between the skull and atlas or between atlas and axis.
bones.source: grays1918:from the axis to the sacrum

bones.name: c7disc
bones.function: Fibrocartilaginous pad between the bodies of C7 and T1 at the cervicothoracic junction, one of the chief bonds of connection between the vertebrae: an annulus fibrosus of concentric fibrous laminae around an elastic nucleus pulposus, bound in front and behind to the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments and acting as a shock absorber between neck and trunk.
bones.source: grays1918:are interposed between the adjacent

bones.name: t1disc
bones.function: Fibrocartilaginous pad interposed between the adjacent surfaces of the bodies of T1 and T2: an annulus fibrosus of concentric fibrous laminae around an elastic nucleus pulposus, serving as a shock absorber and bond of connection. Thoracic discs are of nearly uniform thickness (the anterior concavity of this part of the column is owing to the shape of the vertebral bodies, not the discs) and are proportionally thinner than cervical or lumbar discs, so this region has less pliancy and freedom of movement. Laterally it is joined, by the interarticular ligaments, to the heads of the pair of ribs (rib 2) that articulate with the margins of both vertebral bodies and with the disc between them.
bones.note: The heads of the typical ribs articulate with the discs as well as the vertebrae; the first, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth ribs are the exceptions, each articulating with a single vertebra only — so rib 1 does not reach this disc, but rib 2 does.
bones.source: grays1918:with the intervertebral fibrocartilages between them

bones.name: l1disc
bones.function: Fibrocartilaginous pad interposed between the adjacent surfaces of the bodies of L1 and L2: an annulus fibrosus of concentric fibrous laminae around a soft, highly elastic nucleus pulposus which is especially well-developed in the lumbar region. Lumbar discs are thicker in front than behind, contributing to the anterior convexity (lordosis) of the loins, and under pressure the nucleus flattens and broadens against the fibrous laminae — the column's principal shock absorbers.
bones.source: grays1918:especially well-developed in the lumbar region

bones.note: Taken together the intervertebral fibrocartilages constitute about one-fourth of the length of the vertebral column (excluding the first two vertebrae), the cervical and lumbar regions holding proportionally the greatest share — hence their greater pliancy.

bones.note: The nucleus pulposus is the remains of the notochord — a persistent trace of the embryonic axial rod at every disc level.
bones.source: grays1918:especially well-developed in the lumbar region

bones.name: l5disc
bones.function: Fibrocartilaginous pad between the body of the last lumbar vertebra (L5) and the upper surface of the body of the first sacral vertebra — the lumbosacral disc, the lowest of the series that extends from the axis to the sacrum. Like its fellows it is an annulus fibrosus of concentric fibrous laminae around an elastic nucleus pulposus, thicker in front than behind, and it carries the whole weight of the trunk into the sacrum and pelvis.
bones.note: Sits at the lumbosacral junction, where the base of the sacrum projects forward and forms the prominent sacrovertebral angle with the last lumbar vertebra.
bones.source: grays1918:from the axis to the sacrum
